text:
marie: Quick profiling pass on Llama-2-13B + Mixtral draft pairing. Seeing an ~18-25% perf regression when RoPE scaling flag is enabled on the Mixtral path. Dumping the short log below.
kevin: Can you paste the perf numbers? kernel names, batch sizes?
marie: Sure — here's the hotspot from `rd-prof` (p95/p99 per-token ms):
```
model                 kernel_selected        batch=1   batch=8   batch=16
llama-13b             matmul_opt_v2          1.8ms     0.6ms     0.5ms
mixtral-8x            generic_matmul         2.4ms     1.2ms     0.9ms  <-- fallback
mixtral-8x (rope on)  rope_kern_v1           3.1ms     1.4ms     1.1ms
qwen-7b-draft         token-shard_kern       1.5ms     0.5ms     0.4ms
```
marie: Note: acceptance rate for using the draft model (Qwen) with Mixtral base was ~0.62 in the baseline. Lowering speculative acceptance threshold to 0.55 increased acceptance to ~0.83 but raised p99 tail by ~12ms.
ria: Hmm tokenizer mismatch between Qwen and Mixtral could explain low acceptance — tokenization length drift observed in samples.
kevin: Any kernel selection logs? runtime might pick generic path because tile dims don't match optimized kernels.
marie: runtime log shows `selected_kernel=generic_matmul; reason=tile_mismatch(shape=(64,768))` at 1769804325 — that's the exact fallback.
samir: Are heads/kv-dim assumptions correct for Mixtral? If runtime uses wrong kv stride we'll trigger fallback.
dmitri: We saw similar for Mistral — remote compile picks matmul ops with T=32 vs expected T=64. Mixtral per-head dim=64 requires kernel_v3. If kernel_v3 missing, fallback occurs.
marie: Quick mitigation I tested locally: pin `kernel_version=v3` for mixtral and disable `rope_scaling` for short sequences. Results: batch=8 p99 dropped from 1.4ms -> 0.7ms; acceptance rate stayed ~0.62.
kevin: So enabling RoPE scaling triggers a kernel path not implemented/optimized for Mixtral -> slower kernel. We should add kernel-selector rule: prefer `rope_kern_v2` only when `head_dim % 64 == 0` and `seq_len > 512`.
ria: Also add tokenizer-pairing heuristic: if tokenized length ratio > 1.05, reject pairing automatically (to avoid wasteful speculative runs).
samir: For speculative decoder acceptance: include normalized logprob delta + token-length-ratio penalty in the acceptance function. In my local runs that increased acceptance without a big latency hit.
marie: I pushed a tiny PR with kernel rule + tokenizer ratio check: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4521 — CI perf tests show improvement on nightly for Mixtral.
ops-bot: deploy ci/nightly-mixtral succeeded :rocket: (build 4521)
dmitri: Follow-ups: (1) add kernel profile tests to catch generic_matmul fallback, (2) add draft-pairing unit tests that run tokenization concordance, (3) perf-regression alert for 15%+ p95 increase per model-family.
kevin: Also add a perf gate on rollouts: speculative acceptance default conservative for new pairings until we have 1k in-prod requests.
marie: I'll open tickets for the three items and add a tiny benchmark harness for token-length-ratio. Posting a quick reproduction command for anyone who wants to run locally:
```
# repro: runs a small load to trigger selector fallback
rd-bench --model mixtral-8x --seq-len 1024 --batch-sizes 1,8,16 --rope-scaling on --trace-kernel-selection > mixtral_trace.log
rd-prof --from-log mixtral_trace.log --format table
```
ria: One more note — quantization profile for Mixtral changes tile boundaries. We should add a quantization-aware kernel match in selector (q-aware kernels).
marie: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll file the action items and coordinate with infra to get kernel_v3 added to the runtime build matrix.
